object: Graffito, three short lines engraved between double rules over a Romano-Egyptian figure of a king offering (the 'Pharaoh of Senemt' or Biga), lowest register, west end of the south wall of the passage; 31 x 9.6 cm; squeezes Lepsius and Borchardt, photo no. 479; L., D. VI Bl. 1 no. 3; Pls. XXXV-XXXVI
site: Philae, Gate of Hadrian, passage walls (south wall)
text_std: yeseboẖe tniqo : qoro : mret | mete : tlo : wos selo :
text_corpus: yesboXe tniqo qoro mret mete tlo woS slo
notes: Griffith prints ONE composite text for the two nearly identical graffiti 119 and 120 ('The texts give', p. 45, two type lines: 'yeseboẖe tniqo : qoro : mret | me(y)te : tlo : wos selo :'), with the y of me(y)te in parentheses; his note 'and 120 seems to give' te-y-e-m (meyte) shows the y belongs to 120 only, so this row is the composite without the y (mete). Griffith: 'They are carelessly written and leave several points doubtful.' The first word (yeseboẖe) is 'a title or description found on the lion-bases of Meroe (Meroe 7, 9), and above in 94/2, as well as at Shablul'; 'It might here be part of the name compounded with' mni, 'but' tni 'seems the better reading' (Tani, a name in Kar. 89 and in that of the prince on the Ammon temple at Naga). qoro 'seems to be the royal title spelt as in no. 69 (Meroe no. 12c)'. His '?' is printed over the m of mret, and 'The next might be read' tret. wosselo 'belonging to Isis' (cf. 'belonging to Ammon' in 98). Re-checked at 4x: the 3-sign of yeseboẖe is the wide angular ẖ; those of mret and me(y)te are the narrow smooth m; the s of wos is the closed 3 (s). Griffith's English rendering is not given (names only). The type lines are Griffith's, not the stone's (each graffito has three short lines). Condition (Griffith): the squeezes show it complete, but the surface deteriorated, especially on the left of the top line; in the photographs the top line is nearly hidden by cement. ' | ' marks each line of Griffith's type (he sets one phrase per type line; an overflow printed right-aligned on the next line is joined to its line); (n) is his superscript stone-line number, kept where printed; [x] his restoration; [.] a lost sign (hatched); [...] his dots.

object: Fragment of a round-topped granite stela (most of the left half): half of a winged disk, a winged uraeus crowned with the sun's disk, part of a kneeling figure adoring it; below, the ends of ten lines of transitional cursive between rules; lower end lost; Pl. XLI
site: Provenance not stated (Griffith links the names to the royal trio of the Lion temple at Naga); Moscow, formerly Golenischeff collection; read from the late owner's photograph
text_corpus: ... ntkmni ... mnitore ... arkxror ... mN xrpxeN ... w yeqe ... te nteN ... qedi te ... ... debNqo ... xrpxeN ... mkli ...
notes: Griffith says ends of ten lines; his superscript numbers 2 to 11 are printed, each before the lost beginning of its line (the left half survives, so every line keeps only its end). Here ' | ' marks his six printed rows, which run on from line to line; the stone lines are the (n) marks. Griffith: the first three lines held the names and titles of Natakamani (ntkmn[i]), Amanitere (mnitor[e]) and [A?]rakakharer ([a]rkḫror); his footnote: the loss of the first letter of the prince's name and the absence of i after r leave some doubt about the identification. ll. 5-9: 'The well-known title kharpkhen seems probable' (ḫrp(5)[ḫeñ] and [ḫr]pḫe(10)[ñ]); yeqe 'occurs on the Isis from Napata, no. 75'; qedi 'is a title'; l. 8 'probably ended with a proper name' (debñqo). His queries ('?' printed over the sign): q of qedi; both restored signs of [ḫr]pḫe; the divider after mkli. His restorations: [i], [e], [:], [a], [ḫeñ], [ḫr], [ñ]. Checked at 4x: every 3-sign here is the narrow smooth m (ntkmni, mnitore, mñ, mkli); k has the angular Z top (ntkmni, arkḫror, mkli), p the rounded top (ḫrp, pḫe); in yeqe the q is the single q sign (stroke + ɔ), not o + q; to in mnitor[e] is the barred hook with the dot below. Space kept as printed in 'qedi te'. ' | ' marks each line of Griffith's type (he sets one phrase per type line; an overflow printed right-aligned on the next line is joined to its line); (n) is his superscript stone-line number, kept where printed; [x] his restoration; [.] a lost sign (hatched); [...] his dots.

object: Upper half of a statuette of a lion-headed god (presumably Apedemak; crown and both arms lost), blackish sandstone; part of an inscription in archaic characters in two columns on the back pilaster; Pls. XLI, XLIV
site: Provenance unknown (obtained a few years before 1912 in Cairo); Louvre; read from a cast sent by M. Bénédite
text_corpus: ... dqrid bi tNyidmni ... ... t ym. kdem ...
notes: Two columns, printed as two rows; (2) is Griffith's superscript 2 at the head of the second column; his dots mark the lost parts, and the single dot before m in the second column is read as one lost sign. tñyidm[ni] is the royal name Tanyidamani. Griffith: 'The writing is obscure': two other readings 'would be possible' (his type: i-r and two strokes, and debi 'with inserted e'), 'but' dqri and 'dmni tñyi' 'both occur in Meroe 5/6; cf. also' tñyiñ, ib. 7/13, Kar. 92. 'In the second column' m + [se] (the y read as se with its J restored) 'might be read, and the last letters (cf. Meroe, no. 23) may be intended for' pdem[k], '(A)pazemek, the name of the Lion-god'. The type itself has k (angular Z top, checked at 5x beside the rounded p of his note and of no. 126) at the head of that group, so it is transcribed kdem. His queries ('?' over the sign): the d of tñyidm[ni]; the d after qri; the q; the restored [d]; and in the second column the m of kdem. 3-signs all narrow smooth m (checked at 5x). ' | ' marks each line of Griffith's type (he sets one phrase per type line; an overflow printed right-aligned on the next line is joined to its line); (n) is his superscript stone-line number, kept where printed; [x] his restoration; [.] a lost sign (hatched); [...] his dots.

site: Provenance not stated; Römisches Museum, Hildesheim (marked as given by J. Dümichen); cast in the Berlin Museum, G. 392
notes: Griffith does not print the text: only the groups quoted in his commentary are transcribed, in his order. (a) face A: l. 1 [.]teqo :, 'which may be the end of the principal name'; l. 4 [.]tḫl : nt[.]; l. 5 [.]bd ñk[.]. (b) face B: l. 1 [.]ttoto :; l. 2 [.]qedi se[.], 'apparently the name of Aqezis, i.e., Khons'; l. 3 telm :. Here ' | ' separates the quoted lines and [.] is his hatched block (damage, length unknown). Face A: 'Very little writing remains.' Face B: the bad engraving of the lower lines robs us of several signs; a hard quartzy vein resisted the graving tool in parts of ll. 3-5. 'It is impossible to say whether this was a funerary monument or otherwise.' His queries: '?' over te in face A l. 1; '?' before k in face A l. 5; in face B l. 3 two '?' printed between m and l and between l and te.
